subject: Request: Temporary coverage for SOC 2 Type II audit gap
body:
From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@novushealth.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: procure@novushealth.com
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Audit coverage question and temporary coverage request

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking this — quick background: NovusHealth's procurement team is reviewing Redwood for a critical integration. We require a SOC 2 Type II report that covers the period through the end of 2026. I was able to download the 12/31/2026 report from your portal, but Procurement has flagged the gap between that report end date and our expected go-live of June 2027.

Before we proceed to contract language, Procurement asks whether Redwood can provide a short "temporary coverage" or bridge letter that: 1) confirms there have been no material changes to your control environment since 12/31/2026, and 2) lists any control exceptions or remediation activity in the interim. They also requested an ETA for when your next Type II report will be available.

Can you confirm whether Redwood issues bridge letters for post-report gaps and, if so, share an example/templated letter and expected turnaround? Procurement would like a written assurance to keep the deal cadence moving.

Appreciate it — Jordan
Jordan Ellis
Head of Vendor Risk
NovusHealth

-----Original Message-----
(attachments: none)

On Sun, 9 May 2027 at 10:05 AM Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com> wrote:
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@novushealth.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit coverage question and temporary coverage request

Jordan — thanks for the clear note. Short answer: yes, we provide a bridge-style affirmation for customers that explains the audit period, any known post-period work, and confirms no unreported material control regressions.

Looping in Lauren (Head of Compliance) to confirm the language and Marissa on the commercial side to keep Procurement aligned. Lauren — can you confirm whether we can issue a tailored bridge letter for NovusHealth that includes a short control summary and sign-off? Also: Jordan asked for ETA on the next Type II — we expect the next report to complete Q4 2027 (fieldwork currently scheduled late summer).

Rishi
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit coverage question and temporary coverage request

Rishi / Marissa — I reviewed NovusHealth's ask and drafted a focused bridge letter that addresses: scope (SOC 2 Type II controls), report period (ended 2026-12-31), statement of no material changes to control environment, and a short appendix that discloses minor remediation work in Q1 2027 (low-severity configuration drift on a non-production logging pipeline; remediated on 2027-03-14).

Notes for the draft:
- I kept the language limited and factual, avoiding forward-looking guarantees.
- Signed by our Head of Compliance and timestamped with today's date.
- Included an excerpt listing the control domains covered (CC1-CC7) and a paragraph about our continuous monitoring practices and vulnerability management cadence.

I've attached the draft bridge letter (redwood_bridge_letter_draft_20270510.docx). Please review — Marissa, confirm whether we should include any contractual language or if we want to push Procurement to accept the letter as an interim artifact prior to contract signature. If Procurement requires more evidence, we can also supply the SOC 2 report PDF and our System Description excerpt.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Compliance
Redwood Inference

(attachment: redwood_bridge_letter_draft_20270510.docx)

-----Original Message-----
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit coverage question and temporary coverage request

Lauren — looks good. Two quick asks from Procurement perspective:
1) Can we include a brief bullet confirming SLAs / incident reporting obligations have not changed since 12/31/2026? That typically calms procurement reviewers.
2) Add a line describing where evidence (SOC report PDF, control maps) can be downloaded or viewed (we should prefer a secure link or NDA gating).

If you can add those two lines I think we're ready to send. I'll draft a short covering email and propose a DocuSign flow if they need a signed acknowledgement.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@novushealth.com>
Cc: procure@novushealth.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit coverage question and temporary coverage request

Jordan — thanks again for the note and patience. Attached is our bridge affirmation for NovusHealth. Highlights:
- Confirms the SOC 2 Type II report covering the period to 2026-12-31 (attached as PDF for convenience).
- States that no material changes to Redwood's control environment have been identified since the report end date.
- Discloses one minor remediation (non-production logging pipeline) completed 2027-03-14; no impact to production controls.
- Includes a short statement on our monitoring & patch cadence and contact for evidence requests.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026-12-31.pdf (SOC 2 report), redwood_bridge_letter_final_20270511.pdf (signed by Lauren Bishop)

If Procurement wants the letter on a DocuSign flow, please sign here and confirm receipt: https://docusign.com/link/abcdef123456
Alternatively, reply to this thread confirming the letter meets your requirements and we will mark it for your account.

If you need additional evidence (test procedures, SysDesc excerpt), Lauren is copied and can provide a secure link per NovusHealth's access rules.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

(attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026-12-31.pdf, redwood_bridge_letter_final_20270511.pdf)

-----END OF THREAD-----
